defect: When two slots of one system's top 10 resolve to the same doc_key through the pool's alias table, the published scorer gave each slot the paper's gain and counted each towards P@10, while the ideal ranking uses unique papers, so nDCG@10 could exceed 1.
rule: A paper's second and later appearances in one ranked list score as not relevant (gain 0). Positions are unchanged; precision_of_returned keeps the number of slots returned as its denominator; the oracles are built from the corrected per-arm values. Hit@1, Hit@10 and MRR@10 come from target_rank, the first appearance, and do not change.

repeated_slots.match_definition: Each repeated slot is compared with the first slot holding the same paper: same_doi, the two hits carry the same normalised DOI (one record returned twice); pmid_alias, different or missing DOIs but the same PubMed id; title_alias, neither identifier shared but the same normalised title (first 120 characters), which is how the pool's union-find joined them; transitive, joined only through a third record.

known_item_metrics_unchanged.why: They are computed from target_rank, the first position at which the target's DOI or PubMed id appears (rankOfTarget in run-final-retrieval.mjs), and never from grades.
